A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LM-CC research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material relocated in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original complexity-performance correlations, code-rewriting experiments, and a weighting-factor ablation in Tables 1–3 and Figure 3.

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations across models, code summarization, decomposition ablations, and computation-time measurements in Tables 2 and 4–6.

M1.justification: The entropy-and-syntax segmentation, BFS hierarchy construction, and weighted aggregation of TotalBranch and TotalCompLevel remain unchanged. Equation 4 and Algorithm 1 are retained; additional entropy backbones and ablated variants expand evaluation without changing the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluated code summarization in Tables 2, 4, and 6, extending task coverage beyond program repair, Python-to-C translation, and execution reasoning. The original xCodeEval and HumanEval tasks remain. The summarization dataset is not identified, although the added task coverage is explicit.

E2.justification: Table 5 introduces syntax-only and entropy-only decomposition variants as evaluated comparators against full LM-CC. The existing CC, HC, MI, CoC, and component-feature comparisons are retained. Additional entropy estimators and task-performing LLMs are experimental configurations rather than new competing complexity metrics.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from CodeLlama alone to four entropy estimators and adds GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3.5-122B task performers alongside DeepSeek-V3. V2 also introduces decomposition controls and per-sample timing measurements. The original length-controlled correlation procedure, alpha and tau settings, and rewriting selection protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New decomposition ablations test the contributions of entropy boundaries and syntax-guided structuring, addressing whether the hybrid construction is necessary (Table 5). V2 also adds analyses of dependence on entropy/task models and computational cost. The original weighting-factor ablation is preserved and relocated to Appendix E.2.

E5.justification: Both versions apply the same significance threshold and select the strongest significant grouped correlation across 9–11 groups (Appendix C). V2's significant-correlation ratios summarize additional outcomes without introducing a new uncertainty-estimation procedure. No new seed information, repeated-run protocol, confidence intervals, or significance tests are documented.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial correlation, decomposition-ablation, and timing results in Tables 2 and 4–6. The original three CodeLlama/DeepSeek-V3 correlation rows remain unchanged. Table 3's execution-reasoning original/rewritten scores change from 97.8%/98.3% to 94.1%/95.0%, and rewritten LM-CC changes from 9.4 to 9.3. These are revised reported results; no explanation or protocol revision establishes their cause.

T1.justification: V2 adds a brief argument claiming O(n) token complexity from single-forward-pass entropy computation in Appendix E.3 and frames Assumption 3.2 around semantic rather than control-flow divergence. The principal equations, Theorem 3.3, Corollary 3.4, and Appendix B propositions and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: traditional metrics inadequately capture LLM difficulty, LM-CC measures semantic nonlinearity, and reducing it improves downstream performance. Shortened contribution bullets and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 acknowledges that LM-CC does not always yield the strongest individual coefficient, hypothesizes that entropy-model capacity and calibration explain differences, and attributes ablation benefits to the hybrid hierarchy. Appendix E.3 adds a latency-versus-expressiveness tradeoff. The original semantic-nonlinearity interpretation and proposed applications remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a source-code access URL, identifiers and links for additional entropy models, and disclosures about single-pass computation, mini-batching, and per-sample timing. Existing pseudocode, rewriting prompt, attempt count, temperature, and filtering details remain. Summarization dataset/scoring details and timing hardware are not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 removes the AVATAR citation by Ahmad et al. and the DeepSeek-Coder reference by Guo et al., while retaining the main research positioning. Publication updates for works such as CodeMind and LongCodeZip concern matched existing works. Appendix E.2 more explicitly locates novelty in the LLM-aligned hierarchy rather than depth and branching themselves.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, method explanations, and experimental discussion. It moves the weighting-factor study and Implications section into appendices, shortens contribution statements, and adds acknowledgements and an impact statement. These constitute substantial language and narrative restructuring beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with a separate perplexity-distribution plot and revised code/hierarchy panels. Table 2 gains entropy-model groupings and significance summaries, and Tables 4–6 are added. Figure 3 retains its plotted results but is enlarged and relocated to Appendix E.2.

improvement.justification: V1 relies on one entropy estimator and one task-performing LLM and lacks controls separating entropy-based from syntax-based decomposition. V2's cross-model evaluations and decomposition ablations substantially strengthen evidence for portability and the hybrid design (Tables 2, 4, and 5). Code-access and cost reporting also improve practical assessability. The unspecified summarization protocol and unexplained Table 3 revisions limit reproducibility, but do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation of the central method.
